The work reports an observation of carrier-doped induced interlayer Antiferromagnetic to Ferromagnetic phase transition in
CrSBr semiconductor. Although electrical control of magnetic phase transition is already studied in the CrSBr system, the
present work demonstrates the CrSBr/Graphene heterostructure-based lateral spin-valve without FM metal contact by
exploiting the interlayer charge transfer caused doping effect induced AFM-FM phase transition. The authors have
established the tunability of spin-valve magnetoresistance (MR) by pure electrical means and try to explain how electrical
means tune the spin polarization. However, the manuscript has the following issues to be addressed. Without addressing
these issues, the manuscript is not suitable for publication in Nature Communications in its current form.
“Local maximum near the T_N ~ 132 K in figure 2c is likely reflecting reduced scattering from spin fluctuations after AFM
ordering”. Authors should explain the correlation between the shift in the characteristic maximum and doping-induced
modulation of magnetic ordering more comprehensively.
The manuscript reported that the interlayer AFM coupling is transformed into interlayer FM coupling after doping. In the
undoped system, CrSBr has an easy axis of magnetization. Is there any change in magnetic orientation after doping induced
AFM-FM transition? This information should be provided, which is crucial for applications.
Magnetic phase transition discussed in the manuscript is an interlayer AFM to FM transition. The intralayer magnetic
coupling is FM in the system. Regarding the lateral Spin valve device design, the channel will always have an intralayer
ferromagnetic coupling. Is it accurate to consider the channel to be completely antiferromagnetic, while the magnetic
moments are intralayer ferromagnetically coupled?
Why the spin-valve behavior is reproducible only when the field sweep is confined within ±0.3 T and not reproducible if the
field sweep is beyond ±0.3 T.
Band structure of the system after doping is required to check whether the materials remain semiconducting after doping or
not. If the CrSBr does not remain semiconducting and become conducting after doping, then it will not be possible to locally
dope the system to device a spin valve with spatially localized graphene contact.
In line 73, the mentioned A-type AFM order is not discussed in Supplementary Note 1 and there is no information about the
magnetic phase in Figure S1, as mentioned in the main text.
In line 97, the b direction should be more clearly stated in connection with the unit cell of CrSBr.
In Figure 1a and 1b, y axis for DOS structure should be (Energy)-(Fermi Energy)
In line 128, increase in T¬C is concluded to arise from electron-doping-enhanced intralayer effective exchange interactions
in CrSBr. However, doping induced an interlayer AFM to FM phase change in the CrSBr, which indicates that doping has a
prominent effect on the interlayer exchange coupling. The role of interlayer exchange coupling on the critical temperature
should also be investigated and discussed.
In line 142, figure 1e is referred in the main text, but there is no Figure 1e in the manuscript.
In line 182, it is mentioned that both electrodes exhibit positive spin polarization and after the critical bias, the two electrodes
acquire opposite spin polarization. How the author evaluated and confirmed the similar or opposite spin polarization of the
two electrodes need to be discussed. Further, the calculation of spin polarization of different heterostructures is not sufficient
to interpret how the spin polarization of the two Graphene contacted electrodes are controlled by electrical means. Their
claim of gate tunable spin polarization reversibility is not established clearly.
Some syntax error in Supplementary note 2.
A more comprehensive discussion on confirmation of the STT effect driven magnetic phase transition in the device
configuration with graphene contacts is required.
Details of the theoretical calculation of intralayer exchange coupling is required.

Review of manuscript # NCOMMS-25-52126-T
Title: Doping-Induced Magnetic Phase Transition Enables All-Electrical Spin Control
in CrSBr
In their manuscript Zhao et al. investigated doping by lithium intercalation and electrostatic gating (?) in few-layer CrSBr
devices with graphene (or Au) contacts by measuring MR and performing theoretical modelling (DFT, Monte Carlo, toy
model for magnetization). They observe an AFM-to-FM phase transition by intercalation doping. They claim that the devices
with graphene contacts form lateral spin valves exhibiting spin transfer torque.
I think that the manuscript is in principle interesting, however, lacks clarity and is difficult to follow for a slightly more general
audience due to use of many buzz words and technical jargon that is not explained. I recommend reconsideration after major
revision and have the following comments:
1. In the abstract, the authors write “in which carrier doping alone drives a reversible, zero-field AFM to ferromagnetic (FM) phase transition”. The authors should add that this is by intercalation doping, which is rather different from regular field effect
doping. Intercalation with lithium also changes interlayer spacing, which itself has a strong effect on magnetic order. There
have been prior studies on intercalation doping in CrSBr (i.e. ref. 33), where AFM-to-FM transitions have also been
demonstrated. What makes the results presented here novel?
2. In the abstract, the authors write “tunability exceeding 100%”. What does that mean? They use this expression several
times without explaining it. In line 260 they state “gate-controlled spin polarization exceeding 100%”. What’s a more than
100% spin polarization? That does not make any sense to me.
3. The authors refer to samples D15, D41, D66 and so on. Renaming their samples as 1, 2, 3, etc or some other more
obvious nomenclature would help with readability.
4. In line 97 onward, the authors write “Previous attempts at gate control using conventional solid dielectrics have induced
only modest changes in the coercive field in thin CrSBr flakes… we employ ionic gating to accumulate higher carrier density
in inducing magnetic phase transition in CrSBr”, which sounds like they are doing something particularly novel here.
However, as mentioned above lithium intercalation doping has already been achieved (i.e. ref. 33), even going to
significantly higher doping densities. This text should be rephrased to better place the manuscript within the state of the art.
5. In line 141 onward, the authors write “Theoretical studies predict strong charge transfer at CrSBr/Gr interface that can
induce an AFM-to-FM transition in thin-layer CrSBr” referencing two articles. I noticed that this statement is not supported by
the cited ref. 16, which does not make any theoretical predictions about charge transfer at CrSBr/Gr interfaces.
6. In line 142 the authors write “(also see Fig. 1e)”, however, there is no Fig. 1e in their manuscript.
7. From line 152 onwards, the authors refer to a gate voltage VG, which is not previously defined and not indicated in any
sample illustrations. Are the authors referring to some undefined global back gate? The authors should clarify their structure
and explicitly state what they are doing. VG should appear in a sample illustration. Do I understand correctly that from line
133 onward the authors are no longer using ionic gating but regular electrostatic gating?
8. Do I understand the authors correctly that they are claiming that CrSBr in contact with graphene is always in a FM state?
If yes, I must disagree. See for example ref. 16 (supplementary Fig. 7). Contact to graphene does not just change the magnetic
order in CrSBr. Under certain conditions, probably.
9. Could it be that the state “2” the authors observe in Fig. 3c is simply a sign of layer-by-layer spin flip transitioning from one
AFM order to the other via an intermediate state? This is what it reminds me of. The 0.2 T at which it occurs matches well
with the critical field of the bilayer. See for example Ref. 16 (Fig. 3, optical study of trilayer) as well as Liu et al., Phys. Rev. B
111, L140417, where they show the MR for different layer numbers with the layer-by-layer spin flips inducing changes in the
MR. Have the authors studied a bilayer CrSBr device? This could give clear evidence of the mechanism, as it cannot show
this layer-by-layer switching but would presumably show the spin valve behavior.

experimentally observed MR sign reversal and the corresponding carrier density at the
transition point (Fig. 4d; Supplementary Note 6).

bilayer CrSBr devices would provide a more stringent test of this mechanism. However,
the fabrication of reliable high-quality bilayer devices remains technically challenging,
and we identify this as an excellent direction for future work.

present work demonstrates the CrSBr/Graphene heterostructure-based lateral spin-valve without FM metal contact by
exploiting the interlayer charge transfer caused doping effect induced AFM-FM phase transition. The authors have
established the tunability of spin-valve magnetoresistance (MR) by pure electrical means and try to explain how electrical
means tune the spin polarization. However, the manuscript has the following issues to be addressed. Without addressing
these issues, the manuscript is not suitable for publication in Nature Communications in its current form.

ordering”. Authors should explain the correlation between the shift in the characteristic maximum and doping-induced
modulation of magnetic ordering more comprehensively.

undoped system, CrSBr has an easy axis of magnetization. Is there any change in magnetic orientation after doping induced
AFM-FM transition? This information should be provided, which is crucial for applications.

coupling is FM in the system. Regarding the lateral Spin valve device design, the channel will always have an intralayer
ferromagnetic coupling. Is it accurate to consider the channel to be completely antiferromagnetic, while the magnetic
moments are intralayer ferromagnetically coupled?

### Reviewer 2

Title: Doping-Induced Magnetic Phase Transition Enables All-Electrical Spin Control
in CrSBr
In their manuscript Zhao et al. investigated doping by lithium intercalation and electrostatic gating (?) in few-layer CrSBr
devices with graphene (or Au) contacts by measuring MR and performing theoretical modelling (DFT, Monte Carlo, toy
model for magnetization). They observe an AFM-to-FM phase transition by intercalation doping. They claim that the devices
with graphene contacts form lateral spin valves exhibiting spin transfer torque.
I think that the manuscript is in principle interesting, however, lacks clarity and is difficult to follow for a slightly more general
audience due to use of many buzz words and technical jargon that is not explained. I recommend reconsideration after major
revision and have the following comments:
1. In the abstract, the authors write “in which carrier doping alone drives a reversible, zero-field AFM to ferromagnetic (FM) phase transition”. The authors should add that this is by intercalation doping, which is rather different from regular field effect
doping. Intercalation with lithium also changes interlayer spacing, which itself has a strong effect on magnetic order. There
have been prior studies on intercalation doping in CrSBr (i.e. ref. 33), where AFM-to-FM transitions have also been
demonstrated. What makes the results presented here novel?
2. In the abstract, the authors write “tunability exceeding 100%”. What does that mean? They use this expression several
times without explaining it. In line 260 they state “gate-controlled spin polarization exceeding 100%”. What’s a more than
100% spin polarization? That does not make any sense to me.
3. The authors refer to samples D15, D41, D66 and so on. Renaming their samples as 1, 2, 3, etc or some other more
obvious nomenclature would help with readability.
4. In line 97 onward, the authors write “Previous attempts at gate control using conventional solid dielectrics have induced
only modest changes in the coercive field in thin CrSBr flakes… we employ ionic gating to accumulate higher carrier density
in inducing magnetic phase transition in CrSBr”, which sounds like they are doing something particularly novel here.
However, as mentioned above lithium intercalation doping has already been achieved (i.e. ref. 33), even going to
significantly higher doping densities. This text should be rephrased to better place the manuscript within the state of the art.
5. In line 141 onward, the authors write “Theoretical studies predict strong charge transfer at CrSBr/Gr interface that can
induce an AFM-to-FM transition in thin-layer CrSBr” referencing two articles. I noticed that this statement is not supported by
the cited ref. 16, which does not make any theoretical predictions about charge transfer at CrSBr/Gr interfaces.
6. In line 142 the authors write “(also see Fig. 1e)”, however, there is no Fig. 1e in their manuscript.
7. From line 152 onwards, the authors refer to a gate voltage VG, which is not previously defined and not indicated in any
sample illustrations. Are the authors referring to some undefined global back gate? The authors should clarify their structure
and explicitly state what they are doing. VG should appear in a sample illustration. Do I understand correctly that from line
133 onward the authors are no longer using ionic gating but regular electrostatic gating?
8. Do I understand the authors correctly that they are claiming that CrSBr in contact with graphene is always in a FM state?
If yes, I must disagree. See for example ref. 16 (supplementary Fig. 7). Contact to graphene does not just change the magnetic
order in CrSBr. Under certain conditions, probably.
9. Could it be that the state “2” the authors observe in Fig. 3c is simply a sign of layer-by-layer spin flip transitioning from one
AFM order to the other via an intermediate state? This is what it reminds me of. The 0.2 T at which it occurs matches well
with the critical field of the bilayer. See for example Ref. 16 (Fig. 3, optical study of trilayer) as well as Liu et al., Phys. Rev. B
111, L140417, where they show the MR for different layer numbers with the layer-by-layer spin flips inducing changes in the
MR. Have the authors studied a bilayer CrSBr device? This could give clear evidence of the mechanism, as it cannot show
this layer-by-layer switching but would presumably show the spin valve behavior.
